defects: hsupr is guarded by `BddBelow s` instead of `BddAbove s`: sSup s is only guaranteed to be the genuine supremum (IsLUB) of s when s is Nonempty and BddAbove; with only BddBelow assumed, sSup s can be an arbitrary junk value for unbounded-above sets, so hsupr does not correctly express 'preserves suprema of sets bounded above' (gold's LeftOrdContinuous, built on IsLUB) — it expresses a different, essentially unrelated/degenerate condition

hinf is guarded by `BddAbove s` instead of `BddBelow s`: sInf s is only guaranteed to be the genuine infimum (IsGLB) of s when s is Nonempty and BddBelow; as stated it does not correctly express 'preserves infima of sets bounded below' (gold's RightOrdContinuous, built on IsGLB)

hypotheses require s.Nonempty and thus omit the empty-set case that gold's IsLUB/IsGLB-based LeftOrdContinuous/RightOrdContinuous implicitly cover (preservation of bottom/top elements when they exist)

overall the produced hsupr/hinf are not equivalent reformulations of LeftOrdContinuous/RightOrdContinuous — the bound swap changes the mathematical content of the hypotheses, not merely their presentation
